Tomitaro Makino (牧野 富太郎, Makino Tomitarō; 24 April 1862 – 18 January 1957) was a pioneer Japanese botanist noted for his taxonomic work.
In what year was Coriolis force discovered?
Coriolis force: In physics, the Coriolis force is a pseudo-force that acts on objects in motion within a frame of reference that rotates with respect to an inertial frame.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Methotrexate: Pfizer. Methotrexate, formerly known as amethopterin, is a chemotherapy agent and immune-system suppressant.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Roughly two-thirds of the 150,000 people who die each day succumb to causes linked to this gradual, damage-driven process of growing older — what is it?
Ageing (or aging in American English) is the process of becoming older.
From a Greek word meaning 'dissection,' which old branch of natural science is paired with physiology to study living things' structure and function?
Anatomy (from Ancient Greek (anatom) 'dissection') is the branch of morphology concerned with the study of the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts.

Which plant family of about 181 genera and 2,600 species, nearly all found in the tropics, includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms with large fan- or feather-shaped fronds atop mostly unbranched stems?
Arecaceae are a family of perennial, flowering plants in the monocot order Arecales.

Manufactured by a Turkish company and credited largely to a former MIT graduate, this medium-altitude combat drone has become one of the most exported unmanned aircraft of its era — what aircraft (family) is it?
Baykar Bayraktar TB2 is a family of medium-altitude long-endurance (MALE) unmanned combat aerial vehicles (UCAV) capable of remotely controlled or autonomous flight operations.
A child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, which Frenchman later traded letters with Fermat on probability and built early calculating machines?
Blaise Pascal (19 June 1623 - 19 August 1662) was a French mathematician, physicist, inventor, philosopher, and Catholic writer.

Naturally green and yellow with scalloped black markings, this small, long-tailed seed-eating parrot native to Australia is bred worldwide in colors from blue to white — which bird, also called a budgie?
Budgerigar (--ree-; Melopsittacus undulatus), also known as the common parakeet, shell parakeet or budgie, is a small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot native to Australia.

Born in London and raised in Milan, this Italian Catholic teenager taught himself computer programming and web design to promote devotion to the Eucharist online before his death in 2006 at age 15 — who was he?
Carlo Acutis (3 May 1991 - 12 October 2006) was an English-born Italian Catholic teenager known for his devotion to the Eucharist and his use of digital media to promote Catholic devotion.
Often preceded by a gallbladder attack and typically caused by a gallstone lodging in the cystic duct, which condition can progress to complications like gallstone pancreatitis?
Cholecystitis is inflammation of the gallbladder. Often gallbladder attacks (biliary colic) precede acute cholecystitis.

The most widely distributed corvid, this large all-black bird is found across the Northern Hemisphere and is the heaviest passerine bird, with 11 accepted subspecies showing little variation in appearance. What bird is this?
Common raven (Corvus corax) is a large all-black passerine bird.
This transdisciplinary field studies circular causal processes like feedback and recursion, where an action's outcome becomes the input for the next — what field is it?
Cybernetics is the transdisciplinary study of circular causal processes such as feedback and recursion, where the outcomes of actions return as inputs for subsequent actions.
Domesticated over 14,000 years ago — before farming even began — this descendant of wolves shares a common ancestor with the modern gray wolf. What animal is it?
Dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of wolves.
This is the earliest developmental stage of a multicellular organism, beginning with a single-celled zygote formed just after fertilization — what is it called?
Embryo is the initial stage of development for a multicellular organism.
Known for thin, tapered wings built for high-speed flight and rapid turns, this genus of roughly 40 raptor species includes types called hobbies and kestrels — what are they?
Falcon are birds of prey in the genus Falco, which includes about 40 species.
After working in Feynman's group on the Manhattan Project, this physicist later co-detected a famously elusive elementary particle, winning the 1995 Nobel — who was he?
Frederick Reines (March 16, 1918 - August 26, 1998) was an American physicist.
The simplest stable amino acid, with just a single hydrogen for a side chain, it's the only common one that isn't chiral and makes up about 35% of collagen — what is it?
Glycine (symbol Gly or G) is an organic compound with the formula C2H5NO2, and is the simplest stable amino acid, distinguished by having a single hydrogen atom as its side chain.
This wingless insect spends its entire life on the human scalp, feeds only on blood, and has legs too short and stumpy to jump or even walk well on a flat surface — what is it?
Head louse (Pediculus humanus capitis) is an obligate ectoparasite of humans.
Native to Japan, this deciduous shrub grows big flower heads that can turn pink or blue and is also known as the mophead or lacecap — which plant?
Hydrangea macrophylla is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydrangeaceae, native and endemic to Japan.
Lasting anywhere from a few days to over a month, this disorder makes it hard to fall or stay asleep, leaving daytime drowsiness, irritability and trouble focusing in its wake — what is it?
Insomnia is a sleep disorder causing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep for as long as desired.
This English scientist's 1808 book proposed that elements consist of identical atoms combining in fixed whole-number ratios, laying the groundwork for modern atomic theory — who is he?
John Dalton (5 or 6 September 1766 - 27 July 1844) was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist whose work laid the foundations of modern atomic theory and stoichiometric chemistry.
Despite being a kingfisher, this Australian bird rarely goes near water and can grow up to about 47 centimeters long — what is it?
Kookaburra are terrestrial tree kingfishers of the genus Dacelo native to Australia and New Guinea, which grow to between 28 and 47 cm (11 and 19 in) in length and weigh around 300 g (11 oz).

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.

A chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12, it's a shiny gray metal with low density and high chemical reactivity that readily reacts with air to form a thin passivation oxide coating. What element is this?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12. The free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
First isolated from a cow's pineal gland in 1958 because it could lighten the skin of frogs, this nighttime hormone went on to become famous for governing the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin is a natural compound produced by various organisms, including bacteria and eukaryotes.
With over 86,000 living species spanning sea, freshwater, and even land, this is the largest of all marine phyla — what is it?
Mollusca is a phylum of protostomic invertebrate animals, whose members are known as molluscs or mollusks.

What term, coined in the mid-19th century and often attributed to pathologist Rudolf Virchow, describes the premature death of cells in living tissue due to external injury or infection, as opposed to programmed cell death?
Necrosis (from Ancient Greek (nkrsis) 'death') is a form of cell injury which results in the premature death of cells in living tissue by autolysis.
Despite the zebra-like stripes on its legs, this shy mammal of the northeastern Congo is actually the giraffe's only living cousin — and the sole other member of the family Giraffidae. What is it?
Okapi (Okapia johnstoni), also known as the forest giraffe, and zebra giraffe, is an artiodactyl mammal that is endemic to the northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo in central Africa.

This inflammation of the skin around the nail is often triggered by frequent hand washing or cuticle trauma like nail biting, and is treated with antibiotics or antifungals depending on the cause — what condition is it?
Paronychia is an inflammation of the skin around the nail, often due to bacteria or fungi.

Associated with the early 20th century, this philosophical movement tries to objectively describe subjective conscious experience exactly as it appears, without assuming anything about the outside world — which movement?
Phenomenology (philosophy) is a philosophical study and movement largely associated with the early 20th century that seeks to objectively investigate the nature of subjective, conscious experience.

It plays out everywhere from the clans of traditional societies up through modern governments, and its practitioners negotiate, make laws, and sometimes wage war; what is this activity of settling a society's affairs?
Politics is the activity of settling affairs in an organized society. Politics is usually concerned with resolving issues within a society via a government.
Its biological practitioners link it to neuroscience while its social scientists study groups, all in service of studying the mind and behavior — what is this academic discipline?
Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Psychology is an academic discipline of broad scope, crossing the boundaries between the natural and social sciences.

This genus of roughly 60 herbaceous perennials in the buckwheat family includes the familiar pie vegetable prized for its tart stalks despite mildly toxic leaves — which genus, native to Europe and Asia?
Rheum (plant) is a genus of about 60 herbaceous perennial plants in the family Polygonaceae.
This grayish-leaved, purple-flowered evergreen subshrub is a Mediterranean member of the mint family, long used both as a culinary herb and an ornamental garden plant — what plant is it?
Salvia officinalis is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
Before becoming the first woman on Facebook's board, this executive ran global sales at Google and assisted Lawrence Summers at the World Bank — who later wrote 'Lean In'?
Sheryl Sandberg (born August 28, 1969) is an American technology executive, philanthropist and writer.
Usually diagnosed in infancy, this rare genetic disorder caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene is the leading inherited cause of death in babies if left untreated — what condition is it?
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a rare neuromuscular disorder that results in the loss of motor neurons and progressive muscle wasting.

In the nervous system, this structure lets one neuron send or receive signals with a neighboring cell, and comes in both chemical and electrical varieties — the electrical kind linked directly through gap junctions — name this structure?
Synapse is a structure that allows a neuron to exchange (receive or send) signals with another cell in its immediate vicinity.

When a piece of this obstruction breaks free and travels through the body it's called an embolus, and it can trigger a stroke or heart attack — what is the formation of a blood clot inside a vessel called?
Thrombosis (from Ancient Greek (thrmbsis) 'clotting') is the formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel, obstructing the flow of blood through the circulatory system.

This flowering plant in the ginger family is native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, requiring temperatures between 68 and 86°F and high rainfall. Its rhizomes are gathered and can be used fresh or dried for consumption and dyeing — what is it?
Turmeric is a flowering plant in the ginger family Zingiberaceae. Turmeric powder has a warm, bitter, black pepper-like flavor and earthy, mustard-like aroma.
One of the oldest leaf vegetables eaten by humans, this fast-growing aquatic plant in the cabbage family shares its peppery bite with relatives like mustard, radish, and wasabi — what plant is it?
Watercress (Nasturtium officinale) is a species of aquatic flowering plant in the cabbage family, Brassicaceae.
Earning his doctorate in Islamic philosophy at George Washington University under Seyyed Hossein Nasr, this Turkish academic now directs the country's National Intelligence Organization — who is he?
İbrahim Kalın (born 15 September 1971) is a Turkish bureaucrat and academic who is the current director of the National Intelligence Organization (MT).
Nicknamed for the stripes on its legs and body, this day-biting mosquito native to Southeast Asia spreads dengue, yellow fever, and Chikungunya — what is it called?
Aedes albopictus: Species of mosquito. The insect is called a tiger mosquito as it has stripes, as does a tiger.

An anatomist and archaeologist turned TV presenter, she has served as professor of Public Engagement in Science at the University of Birmingham since 2012 and once led the charity Humanists UK — who is she?
Alice Roberts: English academic, TV presenter and author.
First named by Karl Friedrich Burdach in 1822, this paired brain structure tucked in the temporal lobes drives fear, anxiety, and aggression as part of the limbic system. What is it?
Amygdala: Paired structure within the brain temporal lobe.
Originating from the heart's left ventricle, this is the largest artery in the human body, eventually splitting into the two common iliac arteries in the abdomen — what is it?
Aorta: Largest artery in the human body. The aorta distributes oxygenated blood to all parts of the body through the systemic circulation.
Asperger syndrome is no longer a separate diagnosis. What was it merged into?
It was folded into the autism spectrum by the DSM-5 in 2013 and the ICD-11 in 2022, so clinicians no longer diagnose it as a distinct condition.
As the largest member of the grass family, one species of this plant can grow stalks over 46 meters tall and 36 centimeters thick — name the plant?
Bamboo: Subfamily of plants in the grass family.

With arms and tentacles up to 26 feet long held at right angles to its body, this deep-sea cephalopod has been spotted as deep as 6,212 meters — the only one of its kind known to survive the hadal zone. What is it?

Developed in the 1980s-90s to replace an aging Cold War transport aircraft, this large military cargo plane carries forward the name of two earlier piston-engined predecessors, the C-74 and C-124. What is this modern behemoth called?
Boeing C-17 Globemaster III: American four engine military transport aircraft.

Affecting roughly 22% of people worldwide, this oral parafunctional habit — often during sleep and without the person's awareness — can leave you with aching jaw muscles, headaches, and worn-down teeth. What is it?
Bruxism: Grinding or clenching of the teeth.
When this yeast infection strikes the mouth it's commonly called thrush, leaving telltale white patches on the tongue — what is the condition?
Candidiasis: Fungal infection due to any type of Candida.
Also known by the nickname 'catawba,' this genus of flowering trees is native to warm regions of North America, the Caribbean, and East Asia — what genus is it?
Nicknamed 'Vigorous Dragon' and known to NATO as the Firebird, this Chinese delta-wing, canard-design fighter jet has been exported to Pakistan's air force — which aircraft, capable of Mach 1.8?
Chengdu J-10: Chinese multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Patented in 1967, this sympathomimetic drug helps people with asthma and other breathing disorders by acting as a bronchodilator — which substance?
Clenbuterol: Chemical compound which aids breathing.
One of the most intensively studied and intelligent cephalopods, this mollusk ranges from the Mediterranean and English coastline all the way to South Africa — which species?
Common octopus: Species of cephalopod. The common octopus (Octopus vulgaris) is a mollusk belonging to the class Cephalopoda.

Ancient Greek, Chinese, and Indian cultures lacked a concept for this, seeing art as discovery rather than invention, while the Judeo-Christian-Islamic tradition later reserved it for God alone — what mental faculty is this?
Creativity: Forming something new and somehow valuable.
Also known as jimsonweed or devil's trumpet, this poisonous nightshade plant likely native to Central America has been used both in folk medicine and, unpleasantly, as a hallucinogen — which plant?
Datura stramonium: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Nicknamed the 'businessman's trip' in the 1960s for its rapid onset and short duration, which naturally occurring tryptamine hallucinogen has long been used as a ritual entheogen?
Of the 68 species bearing this name, only the Aquilinae are genetically "true" ones — the rest just qualify as any bird of prey big enough to hunt sizeable vertebrates; what's the common name?
Eagle: Large bird of prey. Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This branch of biology and medicine studies the glands that secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream, governing everything from growth to mood and metabolism — what is it called?
Endocrinology: Branch of medicine pertaining to the endocrine system.
Commonly called spurge, this giant plant genus includes the popular Christmas poinsettia and a thorny succulent nicknamed 'crown of thorns' — which genus is it?
A founder of modern topology who also wrote under the playful pen name "Paul Mongré," this German mathematician — Jewish and facing deportation — died by suicide with his family in 1942. Who was he?
Felix Hausdorff: German mathematician (1868–1942). Hausdorff was Jewish, and life became difficult for him and his family after the Kristallnacht of 1938.
This double-layered fold of skin covering the glans is attached by an elastic band called the frenulum and is typically fused in place at birth — what is it?
Foreskin: Retractable fold of skin which covers and protects the glans of the penis.
Nicknamed the 'stomach flu' in the US and Canada, this inflammation of the gut is most often caused in kids by rotavirus and in adults by norovirus — what is it?
Gastroenteritis: Inflammation of the stomach and small intestine.
Occurring mainly in the liver, this metabolic pathway builds new glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help prevent low blood sugar — what is it called?

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can be up to 6% caffeine — double a green coffee bean — making it a staple in Brazilian soft drinks and energy drinks — which plant?
Named for the Greek word for the sun, this element makes up about 24% of the universe's elemental mass and has the lowest boiling point of all — which colorless, odorless gas?
Helium: Chemical element with atomic number 2 (He)
German anthropologist Otto Schoetensack named this archaic human species in 1908 based on a jawbone found near the village of Mauer — then Europe's oldest known human fossil. Which species?

Homo heidelbergensis: Extinct species of archaic human. H. heidelbergensis has been regarded as either the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans; or as a completely separate lineage.
Formed when chlorine dissolves in water, this compound is the main disinfecting agent in chlorine solutions — and your own white blood cells make it to fight off invading germs. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid: Chemical compound. Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
The global network of networks links private, public, academic, business and government networks using which protocol suite?
The Internet is the global system of interconnected computer networks that uses the Internet protocol suite (TCP/IP) to communicate between networks and devices.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?
This French chemist's discoveries in fermentation and vaccination gave us a heat-treatment process that now bears his name and rabies and anthrax vaccines — who was he?
Louis Pasteur: French chemist, pharmacist and microbiologist (1822–1895)
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)
Named in 1883 by a German anthropologist who wrongly believed it was most common among his patients, this bluish congenital birthmark usually fades by puberty — what is it?
Mongolian spot: Type of birthmark. It normally disappears three to five years after birth and almost always by puberty.
Most often triggered by a viral infection and capable of progressing to heart failure or cardiac arrest, which condition involves inflammation of the heart muscle itself?

Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
Unlike its niacin cousin, this form of vitamin B3 treats pellagra without causing skin flushing, and as a cream is used to fade acne scars and reduce hyperpigmentation — what is it?

Symbolized by the Greek letter omega, this SI unit of electrical resistance was named after a 19th-century German physicist and, since 2019, is defined as an exact value based on fundamental constants — what unit is it?
Ohm: SI derived unit of electrical resistance. The ohm (symbol: Ω, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Sold in extended-release form under the brand name OxyContin, this highly addictive semi-synthetic opioid treats moderate to severe pain and brings relief within about fifteen minutes. What is it?
Oxycodone: Opioid medication. It is usually taken orally, and is available in immediate-release and controlled-release formulations.
Carl Linnaeus named this crop 'hypogaea' — Greek for 'under the earth' — because, unlike most legumes, it ripens its pods below ground. What is it?
Peanut: Legume cultivated as a grain and oil crop.
Grouped within the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, this genus contains today's living flamingo species — which genus?
First synthesized in 1940 by bombarding uranium-238 with deuterons at UC Berkeley, this radioactive metal can expand up to 70% in volume when its surface oxidizes — which element?
Plutonium: Chemical element with atomic number 94 (Pu)
Though often mistaken for a true antelope, this hoofed North American mammal is actually the last living member of its own family, and its closest relatives are the giraffe and okapi — which animal?

Pronghorn: Species of North American hoofed mammal. The pronghorn (UK:, US:) (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.
Named for its four heads, this large muscle group covers the front of the thigh and is the sole muscle that extends the knee — what is it?
Quadriceps: Group of human leg muscle.

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.

A Mediterranean shrub in the mint family, this plant bears fragrant, needle-like evergreen leaves and purple, white, pink, or blue flowers — and those leaves are a beloved cooking flavoring. What is it?
Rosemary: Species of plant. It has numerous cultivars, and its leaves are commonly used as a flavoring.
The second largest planet in the Solar System is a gas giant with an average radius roughly how many times that of Earth?
Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second largest in the Solar System after Jupiter. It is a gas giant with an average radius about 9 times that of Earth.
Drawing on fields from anthropology to epidemiology, this scientific discipline studies everything from sexual development in puberty to gender identity and paraphilias — which field of study?
Sexology: Scientific study of human sexuality.
Brittle, translucent, and found in nature as the mineral halite, this 1:1 compound seasons your fries and de-ices your roads. What is it?
Sodium chloride: Chemical compound with formula NaCl.
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Native to Southern Europe and Anatolia, this deciduous tree produces an edible nut that's been used in cooking since ancient times — what is it commonly called?
Sweet chestnut: Species of tree. A substantial, long-lived deciduous tree, it produces an edible seed, the chestnut, which has been used in cooking since ancient times.
Element 117 carries the second-highest atomic number of any known element and is named for a U.S. state where key research institutions sit — which element is it?
Tennessine: Chemical element with atomic number 117 (Ts)
Known as linden, lime, or basswood depending on the region, this genus of about 30 tree species is the only one in its plant family to form ectomycorrhizal fungal partnerships. What genus is it?
Tilia: Plant genus. Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
Feeding exclusively on vertebrate blood across tropical Africa, this biting fly folds its wings completely over its abdomen at rest and spreads trypanosomiasis — which insect?
Tsetse fly: Genus of disease-spreading insects.

Discovered in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist but only confirmed as a new element in 1830, this hard silvery-grey transition metal takes its name from a Scandinavian goddess of beauty — what element is it?
Vanadium: Chemical element with atomic number 23 (V)
Equal to seven days, this standard calendrical period sits between a single day and a month — despite ancient Egyptians preferring a ten-day version, what unit of time is it?
Week: Time unit equal to seven days. The days of the week are often used to set work days, rest days, and holy days.

Named after a 19th-century British scientist but actually first developed by Leonhard Euler in 1727, this mechanical property measures a solid material's stiffness under tension or compression — what is it called?

Young's modulus: Mechanical property that measures stiffness of a solid material. As such, Young's modulus is similar and proportional to the spring constant in Hooke's law, but with dimensions of pressure instead of force per distance.
The symbol for oganesson is Og. Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Thulium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for thulium is Tm. Thulium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tm and atomic number 69.

William Shatner (born March 22, 1931) is a Canadian actor.
In what year was Nina Dobrev born?
Nina Dobrev: Nikolina Kamenova Dobreva (Bulgarian: Николина Каменова Добрева; born January 9, 1989), known professionally as Nina Dobrev ( DOH-brev), is a Canadian actress.
In what year was Burt Reynolds born?
Burt Reynolds: Burton Leon Reynolds Jr. (February 11, 1936 – September 6, 2018) was an American actor.

Mila Kunis: Milena Markovna "Mila" Kunis (born August 14, 1983) is an American actress.

Daniel Craig: Daniel Wroughton Craig ( CRAYG; born 2 March 1968) is an English actor.
In what year was Diane Kruger born?
Diane Kruger (German: [diˈaːnə ˈkʁuːɡɐ], née Heidkrüger; born 15 July 1976) is a German actress.
In what year was Steven Spielberg born?
Steven Spielberg: Steven Allan Spielberg (born December 18, 1946) is an American filmmaker.
In what year did Helen McCrory die?
Helen McCrory: Helen Elizabeth McCrory (17 August 1968 – 16 April 2021) was an English actress.

Moonfall is a 2022 science fiction disaster film co-written, directed, and produced by Roland Emmerich.
In what year was Dogtooth first released?
Dogtooth (Greek: Κυνόδοντας, romanized: Kynodontas) is a 2009 Greek absurdist psychological drama film directed by Yorgos Lanthimos.
In what year was Nimona first released?
Nimona is a 2023 American animated science fantasy action-adventure film directed by Nick Bruno and Troy Quane and written by Robert L.
